## Spinner

Indeterminate loading indicator. `role="status"` exposes a polite live region named by a visually hidden `t('spinner.loading')`; a caller's `aria-label` overrides that name and `aria-hidden` makes it decorative. Consumes semantic tokens only; the ring uses `currentColor`.

## Icon

Semantic glyph rendering the active skin's SVG via `currentColor`. Decorative by default (`aria-hidden`); an `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` makes it a labelled `role="img"`. Both skins' SVGs ship and CSS shows the one matching the `[data-skin]` ancestor (ADR 0020).

## Divider

Rule separating content. Horizontal (default) renders a native `<hr>`; vertical renders a `<div role="separator" aria-orientation="vertical">`, since a native `<hr>` is semantically horizontal-only. Either way it is a semantic separator by default; a caller wanting it purely decorative passes `role="none"` or `aria-hidden` (which also drops `aria-orientation`). Consumes semantic tokens only; the parent layout owns the surrounding spacing, and vertical needs a sized container to fill.

Source: `src/components/atoms/Divider/Divider.tsx`

## Indicator

Inline status dot. The root is a `<span role="img">` named by the required `aria-label` (the state, e.g. "Available"), so the state is never colour-only (WCAG 1.4.1); `intent` only tints the dot. A caller whose visible text already states the state passes `aria-hidden` to make it decorative. `pulse` adds a live halo that stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Heading

Section heading. `level` picks the real `<h1>`–`<h6>` for the document outline; `variantSize` sets the visual size independently, so semantic level and appearance are decoupled. Type is token-driven and reskins across the theme and skin axes (the display serif in neutral, the pixel font in the pixel skin).

## Text

Body and inline text. `as` picks the element (`<p>` block or `<span>` inline). `tone` maps to `--omnia-color-text-primary` or `--omnia-color-text-muted`; the muted tone still meets WCAG contrast. Type is token-driven and reskins across the theme and skin axes, staying sans in both skins.
